sam: small RFC follow-up idea: introduce a lightweight per-prefix epoch token (short-lived) to avoid global leases for sharing. callers pin an epoch and verify at read; if mismatch, they choose block, fallback cold-read, or accept stale. thoughts?
cheng: sounds promising. main worry: races during eviction/hand-off. eviction must bump epoch atomically with marking pages as evictable, otherwise readers can see a stale token.
divya: agreed. model: epoch is a monotonic 64-bit per-prefix counter in residency header. eviction txn: mark tombstone + bump epoch + start grace TTL. readers compare token, if mismatch behavior is caller-defined.
niko: ops perspective: pins must auto-expire and we need pin quotas per-tenant to prevent hotkey abuse. metrics we'll need: pinned_count, pin_age_seconds, token_mismatch_rate, cold_read_rate.
sam: runtime API sketch (very small):
Cache.pin_prefix(prefix, mode="shadow", expect_epoch=None) -> token, epoch
Cache.read_with_token(prefix, token) -> value, token_valid
Check is a single atomic compare on hot path.
cheng: implementation detail: eviction must use a tiny critical section around bump+mark to avoid races; reclaim should wait for grace window (e.g., 5s) to drain inflight holders. also add unit tests for bump atomicity.
divya: also keep metadata compact: epoch (8 bytes) + tombstone_ts per prefix; avoid per-page bloat. and add metric tag "served_epoch" so we can audit which epoch served requests during canary.
niko: Canary plan: route 10% traffic to nodes with token-check+fallback cold-read. collect p50/p95/p99, token_mismatch_rate, and extra cost. Alert if token_mismatch_rate > 0.5% for 5m. also run a chaos test that kills reclaimer mid-bump to ensure safety.
sam: tradeoffs: strong correctness still needs blocking or global quiesce, this makes it configurable per-client and keeps hot path cheap. I'll write RFC addendum with API shapes, metrics, canary steps, and runbook for stuck pins. ops-bot: can you create canary env? :eyes:
ops-bot: deploy request received: env canary-token-proto created (id canary-21).
cheng: after addendum, add microbench comparing blocking vs fallback latency and a unit test proving epoch bump precedes reclaim.
divya: add a short grace-window invariant check in telemetry: if pinned_count > 0 and tombstone_ts < now - grace, emit alert.
sam: thanks everyone, I'll post the addendum and link back here. :thumbsup:
